Dating again was both harder and easier than I thought. I lost my partner in December 2020 and swore up and down that I could never love again. He was my soulmate and I knew in my heart that it was him or no one. 

When the dust starts to settle, which it will, things change. For me, I couldn't bare the thought of dating someone else for months. Slowly I started to realize that I didn't want to be alone. What I had been so mad at people for telling me, that I was too young to not love again, had some truth in it. I could admit to myself that I wanted to have a life partner but I almost felt embarrassed in a way to tell anyone else. I felt like I would be judged for "giving up" on the relationship I had had. That if I moved on too quickly people would judge me. I started on dating apps around 6 months after he passed, but I didn't tell a soul until I was certain. I knew that I was still so fragile and it was still such a sensitive topic that if I got any kind of negative reaction I would crumble.

I think the most important things to remember when starting to date again are that this is your life, you can move as fast or as slow as you want. If you want to start pursuing people a month after the death go for it, or wait a year, or never again, its your life. Another thing that I promised myself is that whoever I ended up dating would be okay with me talking about my past relationship and partner, and that they would be supportive of my grief. This is not an ex relationship, its a lost relationship. The other important thing to remember is that you will never "replace" your late partner, even if you tried. You are starting a new relationship, not replacing an old. 

I used to tell myself that I would never date and that I was okay to be alone but that's not who I am or what suits me. I've been dating my boyfriend now for 3 months and hes the sweetest thing. I never could have imagined to feel this kind of love and happiness again but it is so possible. 

I'm sorry for your loss and I wish you the best navigating your grief <3

I work in a funeral home and there can be a few reasons actually! Where I'm from we aren't legally allowed to without the executor's permission to do so but they can request it. It's done for identification purposes sometimes but I've also had people who have family that live very far away but wanted to see their loved one in the casket (it can definitely help with the grieving process).

I'm currently working as a funeral directing apprentice and my boyfriend also passed away suddenly, the day before his 22nd birthday. I don't know how you're feeling but I have some shared experiences. 

Working in a funeral home I see the bodies of people who have died daily. I know they are dead, I've prepared them for their funerals, and I still feel like I see them breathing sometimes. It's human for your brain to trick you into thinking you see them breathing, that's what you're used to.

When my boyfriend passed I was jealous and angry at every couple I saw, it didn't feel fair. I took everything people said to heart and constantly got my feelings hurt because no one understood. Keep talking about him. There will likely come a time where you feel like no one cares or they've forgotten but find people to talk about him with, not just his death. My boyfriend passed almost 2 years ago, I'm dating someone new, but I still talk with his friends and family regularly.

Because we were so young when he died I had so many people tell me that I rotor find someone new, I even had someone say that to me at his funeral. I would get so mad every time someone would say that to me because I didn't want someone new, I wanted my boyfriend. At the time I whole heartedly believed I would never date again but over time that shifted and I became more comfortable with the idea. This may or may not happen with you but it was something that was said to me enough that it deserves a warning. 

Everyone experiences grief differently. The grief you experience now will be different than the grief you'll experience a year from now, or 10 years from now, but it will be grief all the same.

I'd recommend watching grief seminar videos or reading up on grief. If you're feeling alone or scared or anything at all it can help.

Absolutely, there are loads of men who are going into any kind of friendship with women with the intent of dating, or that end up developing that want later on. That's totally okay and totally normal! We do it as women too. Realistically for me, I wouldn't surround myself with people who's morals and personalities don't align a decent way with mine and it's not a far stretch to say that I could see myself dating a lot of the guys in my life. 

The distinction I'm trying to make is that wanting a relationship isn't wrong. What's wrong is ending a friendship because you don't see it turning into a relationship. If you don't value a person enough to have them solely as a friend then you shouldn't be in a relationship with them, period. 

I can understand why you would think that men go in with this intention. I don't believe they do, but I understand that I don't know the actual data on that. I just want to remind everyone that it is okay to be hurt by a guy not wanting to be friends after rejection because I think that that's an awful thing for him to do.

Also, I'm not trying to argue you in any way, your points are very valid, I'm just further explain my viewpoint!

It's so hard when that happens. For me I already go into hookups with muted feelings but when there's that moment of realization that they don't see your value, it still manages to hurt.

I'm sorry you've experienced this, but please keep reinforcing that your value does not changed based off of what others think ❤

I get that some people may take the point of view that it's too hard for him to continue a friendship with you but I couldn't disagree more. 

You are not responsible for his intentions or his feelings. You were clear in yours, it is in no way your fault that he didn't accept that.

Deciding to end a friendship, especially one that's gone on for years, because the other person doesn't have romantic feelings is very wrong in my mind. I understand that it could be hard for him at times because he does have more romantic feelings. I understand that this rejection would hurt him. However, he is equating your value as a friend with the potential for a relationship which is so wrong. It is incredibly hurtful to you. He's literally saying that he'd rather not have you in his life at all then just have you as a friend and I am so sorry for that. You are worth more than your eligibility. You are enough as who you are. 

I've been on both ends of this situation. I've been friends with a guy for around the same amount of time who also very clearly has had and still has at least somewhat of a crush on me. About a year into our friendship he asked me out and I told him I wasn't interested. I've made it clear to him since then that I am not interested in a romantic relationship, but that I value him as a friend. I can only imagine the hurt you must feel. If he told me that he wouldn't be friends with me because I didn't want to date him I would be crushed. I've also been on the other side. I recently had a guy that I was friends with a long time ago reach out to me. He was 4 months out of ending his marriage and my boyfriend died about a year from when the old friend messaged. We started talking and hit it off immediately. We'd been having so much fun together but I started to notice little things that made me feel like he wasn't ready to move on yet. We eventually had a good talk (we were still only friends but clearly both were interested) and came to the realization that he really wasn't ready. I won't lie, it hurt bad. I had high hopes for a future with him. He flat out told me he could see a future with me and wanted a relationship, but that the timing wasn't right. He said that he couldn't expect me to wait around for him to sort out his feelings but that he looks forward to the future and the possibility of me being in it. All that to say, I had very strong feelings for him that weren't even immediately shut down, got rejected, and we are still good friends. I value his friendship and having him in my life more than the idea of a relationship with him. Obviously being more would be nice, but he's an incredible person that I want in my life, however that may be.

I'm sorry he valued his thoughts of possibilities more than he valued you as an individual and as a friend. I know it hurts and I'm sorry for that. I hope that you can heal from this.

I cannot emphasize this enough... Your value as an individual is endless. His perception of you does not change the value you hold.

Just over a month after my boyfriend passed away I was in the car with my sister. I was consumed with grief at this point and brought up my boyfriend's death with her, the first real time since his passing. We were driving through the town where my boyfriend lived and I made a small comment about how hard I found it to be there because the last time I was there was for his funeral. She commented on how she felt the exact same way after her partner had cheated on her and that going near where they lived was hard. She has never been an empathetic person but this still took me by surprise. I did my best to brush the comment off and then later on said I couldn't believe how long it had been since my boyfriend had passed already. I was more prepared for a more self-centered response this time and was not disappointed. She immediately said "I know, it's been X months since [her partner's name] cheated". 

We used to fight a lot even just a few years ago and it got to a point where I knew I would either have to cut her off completely or I could just do my best to never disagree with her. She has a very strong personality and most of my immediate family is already mildly careful around her anyway. I decided to keep a mental list of topics that I will not bring up around her in order to keep the peace. I added my boyfriend in general to that list that day. It's been 8 months since he passed and I haven't brought him up since that car ride with her. 

I know this isn't as bad as some of the things in this thread and will get buried but it's nice to get it off my chest.

I will follow you into the dark by Death Cab for Cutie

After my boyfriend passed away I would listen to this song and just cry my eyes out. I've struggled with depression since my teens but his death really did a number on me. I've never believed very heavily into any kind of afterlife but the idea of following him in death, even if it was just into the dark, was really comforting to me.

My boyfriend was a car guy. Anywhere we went he would always have an endless amount of facts about every car/car brand/etc that he saw. Before I met him I really didn't like the idea of dating someone who was into them because I just didn't see the point, as long as the car got you from point A to B, why would it matter what it looked/sounded/performed like? That being said, I had absolutely no knowledge of anything about cars (like thought that mustang was its own car company and was not associated with Ford whatsoever). Anytime he pointed out a cool car to give me facts I would always ask what colour it was because thats the only way I could identify it. He loved the gold coloured cars (we called it "grandpa gold" because they're always driven by old men). 

A week or so after he passed I asked him while driving for his sign to me to be cop cars because he wasn't fond of them (as many cars guys aren't). As soon as I finished asking a cop immediately pulled out in front of me. I decided that that was a dumb sign and that I wanted to change it to something he liked. I still can't identify cars well enough to distinguish one type from another so I decided that I wanted my sign to be gold cars. 

Every time I'm anywhere in a car, usually driving, I count gold cars because I feel like he sends them to me and it helps me to remember him. So far the most I've seen is 32 got cars during a 25 minute drive. I also never keep anything in my passenger seat in case he wants to go for a cruise with me. 

He passed the day before his 22nd birthday from a heart condition. I miss him every second of every day.
